page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.xlarge is a general-purpose instance within the sn2ne family, powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via KVM, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory profile of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX and AVX-512 extensions alongside standard hardware encryption support via AES-NI, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache.

The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring external cloud storage volumes for all disk operations, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. In standardized synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields lower-tier results consistent with legacy Broadwell-generation hardware. Geekbench tests record a single-core score of 928.0 and a multi-core score of 2014.0, while PassMark CPU registers 3642.56. Memory bandwidth reflects similar constraints, delivering 21.27 GB/s in large block read tests and 18.88 GB/s in write tests. Static web serving reaches 2.52 GB/sec throughput, and Redis SET operations attain 2.87 million operations per second.

Because computing throughput and memory subsystem speeds are modest compared to newer generation hardware, ecs.sn2ne.xlarge is best oriented toward predictable workloads that do not demand high single-thread velocity or intensive I/O performance. The balanced memory-to-CPU ratio allows it to comfortably host low-traffic web services, utility scripts, internal continuous integration workers, development staging servers, and mid-tier background workers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz and 16.0 GB of RAM. Featuring a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the KVM-based server runs on the x86_64 architecture across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The instance includes no integrated local storage, requiring remote network storage, and is configured with a 2 Gbps network baseline. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the lower percentiles across compute, memory bandwidth, and static web serving tests, reflecting older-generation architecture. While it lacks high-end computational power, its dedicated core allocation offers stability for workloads that do not require aggressive single-thread throughput. The ecs.sn2ne.xlarge instance is suitable for general-purpose workloads, including internal operational tools, lightweight application hosting, background processing queues, and testing environments requiring standard memory footprints.
